subject: Request: Regional burst carveout & temporary p95 measurement adjustment for pilot
messages:
From: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@brightline.health>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@brightline.health
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Concern: morning p95 spikes during ETL window / ask for carveout

Hi Vanessa,

Quick question as we approach pilot: over the past two weeks our telemetry shows repeated p95 spikes for the Hosted API during our daily ETL loads (roughly 07:00-08:30 PT). These are short, repeatable bursts tied to our ingestion window and are causing some UI timeouts for support users.

We love Redwood's latency performance most of the time, but the spikes are a blocker for our go-live next month. Can you or your team confirm if Brightline can get a short-term exception or measurement carveout around the scheduled ETL window for the remainder of the quarter? Specifically we want to understand:

- Whether Redwood can exclude or treat scheduled, customer-initiated batch periods differently from regular traffic for p95 accounting
- The suggested wording and bounds for an amendment (time ranges, max duration, impact to credits)
- Whether this would be a regional carveout (US-west) or something applied globally

We are open to a measured, temporary approach (e.g., 6–8 week pilot with explicit guardrails) rather than permanent changes. Procurement is looping me on the commercial terms.

Thanks — please let us know ASAP; pilot kickoff is 3/8.

— Sandra
Sandra Lee
Director, Platform Engineering
Brightline Health
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@brightline.health>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, procure@brightline.health
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 12:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Concern: morning p95 spikes during ETL window / ask for carveout

Sandra — thanks for flagging this and for the clear ask. We can absolutely take a pragmatic approach here. High-level proposal below; Marcus and Karthik, I’ve looped you for tech/legal guidance and to confirm feasibility.

Proposed temporary approach (pilot / amendment):
- Pilot duration: 6 weeks starting 2027-03-08 (pilot aligns to your go-live).
- Carveout window: Daily scheduled window 07:00–08:30 PT (US-west); treat traffic within that window as a "scheduled-batch" class for measurement purposes.
- Measurement: Maintain p50/p95 commitments outside the carveout; for the carveout window use a burst carveout rule: up to 10 minutes of contiguous high-latency per hour are excluded from p95 aggregation, capped at 2 hours/week.
- Credits: If overall monthly p95 (excluding carveouts) breaches SLA, then standard credit policy applies; carveout itself is not creditable unless exceptions above caps are exceeded.
- Routing: We recommend regional routing (keep Brightline traffic in us-west) during the pilot to limit cross-region variance.

Attachments: I attached a short slide with these bullets (proposed-exception-term-vanessa-slides.pdf). Marcus — could you review the carveout measurement language and the proposed caps? Karthik — can you confirm whether a 6-week pilot and a narrowly-scoped legal amendment will work from procurement/legal perspective?

Next steps: If you agree in principle I can draft a short amendment and DocuSign it for review.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0170
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@brightline.health>, procure@brightline.health
Date: Thu, 25 Feb 2027 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Concern: morning p95 spikes during ETL window / ask for carveout

Thanks Vanessa — dug into the traces Sandra sent over and ran a short analysis against our regional telemetry. Key findings:

- The latency spikes line up with sustained high fan-in from a small set of Brightline ingestion IPs between 07:02–08:10 PT; these generate many long-running tokenized requests that cause transient pressure on the GPU work queue and the KV cache warmup.
- We see head-of-line amplification when these bursts run against multi-tenant pools that also serve interactive traffic.

Suggested technical guardrails (to make the carveout conservative and measurable):
- Enforce an explicit "batch" classification at request-level for scheduled jobs (Brightline passes header X-BR-BATCH: true). Requests labelled as batch will be routed to a separate, isolated pool during 07:00–08:30 PT for the pilot.
- Measurement: compute p50/p95 as hourly aggregates from 5-minute rolling quantiles. Within the 07:00–08:30 carveout window we will apply a 10-minute contiguous exclusion per hour (i.e., if there is a burst we ignore the worst 10 minutes of that hour for p95 computation), maximum 2 hours excluded in any 7-day period.
- Fallback: if isolated pool capacity is exhausted, requests auto-failover to a second-tier dedicated pool with higher cost but preserved throughput; such failovers will be logged and count against carveout caps.

I attached a network trace (network-trace-0225.zip) and a draft of the amendment language for measurement (sla-mod-draft.docx). Two things to confirm with legal/sales: the exact verbiage for the exclusion rule (we can make it event-driven rather than time-based) and whether the credit cap (if carveout bounds are exceeded) is acceptable.

If we adopt these technical guardrails the risk of affecting your interactive callers is small and measurable. Happy to run a replay test into an isolated pool before 3/8.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Lee <sandra.lee@brightline.health>, procure@brightline.health
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Feb 2027 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Final: proposed carveout terms and next steps (DocuSign link)

Sandra / Procurement team — following Marcus's technical validation and Karthik's green light on the process, here are the concrete terms we propose for the 6-week pilot amendment: 

1) Pilot window: 2027-03-08 to 2027-04-19 (6 weeks).
2) Daily carveout: 07:00–08:30 PT, only for requests labelled X-BR-BATCH: true.
3) Measurement: hourly p50/p95 computed from 5-minute rolling quantiles. Within carveout hours, exclude up to 10 minutes contiguous high-latency per hour, capped at 2 hours per 7-day period. Exclusions must be tied to routed-to-isolated-pool events and instrumented.
4) Credit policy: Standard SLA credits apply to breaches outside carveouts. If carveout caps are exceeded, Brightline is eligible for a single pro-rated credit capped at 10% of the monthly Hosted API bill for that billing cycle.
5) Operational: Redwood will enable regional routing to us-west for Brightline during pilot and run a pre-pilot replay test (TBD). Failure to meet the agreed instrumentation or routing conditions voids carveout eligibility.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/req/BR-4792-amendment (draft amendment attached). HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/BR-4792.

If these terms look good I’ll push the amendment for signature and schedule the replay test with Marcus. If you need different carveout windows (e.g., two shorter windows instead of one) say so and we’ll adapt.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
